project_title: Repairs and reconstruction works on 12 culverts Devines Hill, Old Great North Road
project_description: This project will repair and reconstruct 12 culverts on Devines Hill, part of the Australian Convict Sites World Heritage Property. These 12 stone culverts, built by convicts between 1830 and 1832, require repair or reconstruction works to ensure they continue to work effectively to drain water off the surface of the Old Great North Road. The works are informed by the Conservation Management Plan and Maintenance Plan.

project_title: In the Footprints of our Ancestors Willandra Ancient Fossil Trackway
project_description: This project synthesises 20 years of research and through community direction will enhance the preservation and promotion of Aboriginal Culture and Heritage in the Willandra Lakes through an interactive multi-media interpretation of the stories surrounding the 20 thousand year old Willandra Fossil Trackway site.

project_title: National Heritage Values Planning Framework for Broken Hill

project_title: Conservation of the Vulliamy clock at Hyde Park Barracks Museum
recipient: The Trustee for the Historic Houses Trust of NSW
project_description: The Vulliamy clock at HPB is the oldest working public clock in Australia with aesthetic significance for its sound that has resonated across Queen's Square since 1819. The proposed works include clock face, bell restoration; collection management documentation; provision of service program to prevent future damage and safe access for clock winding by staff will ensure its future operation and management.

project_title: Kosciusko Community Conservation
project_description: Community volunteers will be engaged in conservation activities in Kosciuszko National Park (KNP) to address key objectives as identified in the KNP Plan of Management and the strategic plan for the Australian Alps National Parks. The activities include surveying for priority and emerging weeds, Threatened species, feral animals and dieback, and undertaking targeted weed control and site rehabilitation.
nhl_site: Australian Alps National Parks and Reserves

project_title: Monkey Mia Rejuvenation
recipient: Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions
project_description: This project will continue the staged rejuvenation of public visitor facilities in the Monkey Mia Conservation Park as outlined in the Monkey Mia Master Plan. Four critical infrastructure elements will be developed to support the welfare of the visiting dolphins, enhance the visitors' dolphin interaction experience and promote and interpret Shark Bay's World Heritage values.

project_title: Goldfields Water Supply Scheme - No 3 Pump Station Conservation Works
project_description: No 3 Pump Station is one of six remaining pump stations constructed as part of the Goldfields Water Supply Scheme. This project will undertake conservation works required to the fabric of the building and site. The project will contribute significantly to the overall building condition, enhance visitors experience, address potential safety issues and reinstate the building's original architectural aesthetics.

project_title: West Kimberley Wanjina and Gwion rock art
project_description: This project aims to maintain and protect the Wanjina Wunggurr Homeland, associated Wanjina and Gwion rock art (also Makassan sites, log-raft maritime tradition and traditional pearl shell trade sites whilst enhancing visitor experience. A decision-making framework will be established to develop management interventions in consultation with Traditional Owners and the public with initial focus on Bigge Island.

project_title: Cheetup Cultural Management Plan
recipient: Esperance Tjaltjraak Native Title Aboriginal Corporation
project_description: This project will develop and deliver a cultural plan for the Cheetup Rock Shelter; led by the Esperance Nyungar Elders and Tjaltjraak Rangers. The plan will detail the aspirations of the Traditional Owners for culturally-appropriate access, management and use of this place. The cultural plan will then go through a formal process of integration with the existing national park management plan focusing on environmental management protocols combined with visitor management.

project_title: Deep Gorge Art Viewing Trail, in Murujuga National Park
project_description: This project will provide a safe viewing platform to showcase the petroglyphs at Murujuga National Park as well as serve as an area for greater interpretation, such as signage and tours.

project_title: Cross tenure feral animal control in the West Kimberley
project_description: This project will reduce feral herbivore numbers across large areas of the highly biodiverse north west Kimberley. Removal of animals will be from high value areas including around rock art sites, rivers and wetlands and known areas of high biodiversity, and develop a strategy for ongoing work to manage feral herbivores across the region as well as initiate a monitoring program of feral animal impacts on rock art sites in the Wilinggin IPA.
